title: Cancer & uncontrolled division
examples: What causes cells to divide too much?
How are benign and malignant tumours different?
Are there things I can do to lower my cancer risk?

explain.say: Today we are learning about cancer and uncontrolled cell division.

items: Cancer means cells divide too much.
This division is uncontrolled by the body.
It can form masses called tumours.

explain.say: A tumour is a mass of abnormal cells in the body.
Tumours can be benign or they can be malignant.
Malignant tumours are bad because they can spread to other parts.
Some things increase your risk of developing cancer.

items: Smoking tobacco products is a major risk.
Exposure to certain chemicals can increase risk.
Sun exposure without protection is a factor.

explain.say: When you are cycling, your body uses many cells for energy.

faq.q: What is the difference between benign and malignant tumours?
faq.a: Benign tumours are not cancerous and usually stay in one place. Malignant tumours are cancerous and have the ability to spread to other parts of the body.
asks: Can a benign tumour ever become bad?

faq.q: How does cancer start in the body?
faq.a: Cancer starts when cells have faulty DNA, causing them to divide without proper control signals. This faulty division leads to uncontrolled growth.
asks: Is it always due to bad genes?

faq.q: Are there specific foods that cause cancer?
faq.a: There are no specific foods that guarantee cancer. However, maintaining a balanced diet is important for overall health and reducing risk.
asks: Are certain vitamins linked to cancer?

faq.a: Metastasis is the process where cancer cells break away from the original tumour and travel to form new tumours elsewhere in the body.
asks: What does it mean if cancer spreads?

faq.q: Why is smoking a major risk factor?
faq.a: Tobacco smoke contains carcinogens, which are chemicals known to damage the DNA inside the cells. This damage can lead to uncontrolled cell division over time.
asks: What chemicals in smoke are dangerous?

facts: Cancer results from uncontrolled cell growth.
Benign tumours generally do not spread to other tissues.
Malignant tumours can spread through the bloodstream.
Avoiding known carcinogens like tobacco smoke lowers risk.

quiz.say: A growth that remains in one spot and does not spread is called:
quiz.why: Benign tumours are characterised by staying local and not invading nearby tissues.

wrong.1: This is wrong because malignant tumours are the ones that spread.
wrong.2: This is wrong because metastasis is the spreading process, not the name of the growth itself.
wrong.3: This is wrong because normal division is controlled, whereas the question asks for a specific type of mass.

quiz.say: If cancer cells travel to a distant organ, this process is called:
quiz.why: Metastasis specifically describes the journey and establishment of cancer in a new location.

wrong.0: This is too general; it describes any lump, not the act of spreading.
wrong.1: This is a general term for cell division, not the process of spreading.
wrong.3: This is not a scientific term used to describe cancer spreading.

quiz.say: Which of these lifestyle changes helps reduce cancer risk?
quiz.why: Tobacco smoke contains harmful chemicals that damage cell DNA, so avoiding it is key to prevention.

wrong.0: A sedentary lifestyle is associated with increased risk, not decreased risk.
wrong.2: While diet matters, eating only one type of food is not a recommended prevention strategy.
wrong.3: Ignoring sun exposure increases risk because UV rays damage skin cells.
